method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of all five changed blocks, with exact macro, formula, identifier and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Church–Turing thesis as a claim about effective procedures, extensional agreement of formal models, and its two uses for machine existence and impossibility.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Turing machines are intended as a precise stand-in for effective procedures. Other proposed precise models compute the same set of functions, supporting the claim. The thesis says whatever can be computed by an effective procedure is Turing-computable.
samples.checks: The intuitive-versus-formal distinction, extensional same-function-set explanation and thesis direction are preserved; the claim is not recast as a theorem derived from model equivalence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Given an effective procedure in pseudocode, the thesis may justify asserting that some Turing machine computes the same function even without explicitly constructing that machine; the source jokingly calls this an excuse for laziness.
samples.checks: The existence inference, lack of actual construction and source's informal tone are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If no Turing machine computes a function, then by the thesis no effective procedure computes it, since one would imply a machine. The Halting Problem is therefore claimed unsolvable by any effective procedure, not merely by the particular Turing-machine model.
samples.checks: The contrapositive reasoning, all-procedure scope and Halting Problem application remain unchanged.
